title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: 1Password for Agents: agents sign in to sites without ever seeing the password, with a Claude integration and approvals that expire after 30 days (week of Nov 23)
bullets.summary: 1Password now brokers logins for AI agents so the agent gets a session, not the secret; its Claude integration adds an Agentic Mode, and each grant lapses after 30 days unless renewed.
bullets.how: The Construct: Hermes, Cowork and the B9 partner-order runner currently drive logged-in sessions (Signs365, WordPress, Google) with credentials held in browser profiles and files; moving those logins behind a broker gives per-agent grants, expiry and revocation without pasting passwords into prompts. PRAGMA: the cleanest answer to a client's first question, "what happens to our passwords?"

bullets.title: Anthropic puts Claude computer use in beta for Team and Enterprise plans across desktop, web and mobile (Nov 20, rolling out gradually); Claude Code 2.1.330 adds Enterprise Admin Console sign-in and a built-in chart tool
bullets.summary: Org plans can now let Claude operate a computer from any Claude surface, not just a local desktop setup, while Claude Code picks up admin-console sign-in via claude auth login and self-hosted runner settings such as --start-dir.
bullets.how: The Construct: computer use available org-wide means the AP-Agent Mac tasks (Signs365 carts, WordPress fixes) could be triggered from phone or web; set per-app allowlists before turning it on, since a broader surface is a broader blast radius. PRAGMA: a supported, admin-governed path to pitch instead of home-built screen automation.

bullets.title: OpenAI starts a limited test of "Dots" (Nov 21): persistent, always-on agents for some ChatGPT Plus users and eligible Business workspaces
bullets.summary: OpenAI is testing agents that keep running in the background instead of answering one chat at a time, the same always-on pattern Cognition's Devin Bots shipped last week.
bullets.how: The Construct: our edge has been standing agents (Pulse, Hermes workers, the partner-order runner); with the big labs now shipping always-on agents, the moat moves to the business-specific skills and gates we own, not the scheduling. PRAGMA: expect clients to ask why not just use Dots, so lead with integration and verification.

bullets.title: "Formalize or Lose It" (Nov 23): nearly half of supervisory rules in multi-agent runs lived only in prompts, and executable checks caught failures prompt-only supervision missed; Tether 0.4.0 (Nov 22) replays recorded agent runs as tests
bullets.summary: New research plus a new open test harness point the same way: rules an agent must follow should be code that checks the run, and recorded runs can be replayed to assert tools called, final files and step/cost limits.
bullets.how: The Construct: move written gates (done-means-done, claims-truth, print-file guide) from SKILL.md prose into scripts that fail the run, and replay a saved run of each standing agent after any skill edit. PRAGMA: a citable reason to sell verification harnesses, not just prompts.

bullets.title: Wells Fargo changes its online access agreement (effective Nov 24): customers use third-party AI agents at their own risk; JPMorgan, Schwab and Citi already block or limit credential-based agents
bullets.summary: Big US banks are pushing liability for agent logins onto customers and shutting out agents that sign in with a customer's username and password.
bullets.how: Brand 9 Signs: any agent task touching business banking (reconciliation, payments, pulling statements) should go through bank APIs, exports or a bookkeeping connector, not a scripted login; a credential-based bank session may now void protections. PRAGMA: a dated, concrete risk to put in every client's agent-permissions policy.

praxis_lesson: Rules that live only in a prompt are suggestions: this week's research found executable checks catch the failures prompt-only supervision misses, just as labs start shipping always-on agents that run with nobody watching. The Construct should turn each written gate into a script that can fail the run, and replay saved runs as tests after every skill change.
